subject: general
question: Two engines of trains 28 km apart start towards each other at speeds of 23 km/hr and 89 km/hr, respectively. After how much time will they meet each other? (Assume the length of engine is negligible)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the engines are moving towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds.

Relative speed = 23 + 89 = 112 km/hr

Time to meet = Distance ÷ Relative speed = 28 ÷ 112 = 1/4 hours

Time in minutes = 1/4 × 60 = 15 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 15 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance between the two engines = 28 km

Speed of the first engine = 23 km/hr

Speed of the second engine = 89 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (opposite directions) = Speed 1 + Speed 2

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative speed = 23 + 89 = 112 km/hr

⇒ Time taken to meet = 28 ÷ 112 hours

⇒ Time = 1/4 hours

⇒ Time in minutes = (1/4) × 60

⇒ Time = 15 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 15 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: S = |S₁ − S₂|

Average Speed

When equal distances are covered at speeds a and b consecutively, the average speed for the whole journey is given by 2ab ÷ (a + b).

Passing a Stationary Object

The time taken by a train of length L to pass a point-sized object (like a pole or standing man) is calculated using T = L ÷ Speed of Train.
